candidate_reused_not_rebuilt: the S35 candidate install was reused; its two library digests above are the ones recorded by both measurements. No src/ change was made in S36.

promoted_to_l7.workload: torrent_info SHA-1 + restored ext4 payload + corrupted-block CRC
promoted_to_l7.fix: restore now uses partclone's documented -O/--overwrite target path instead of -o on a non-existent path; this avoids the consumer's S_ISBLK-on-uninitialised-stat ENOENT race. The corruption, SHA-1 and payload assertions are unchanged.

promoted_to_l7.workload: evmctl IMA sign/verify with a tampered-file reject
promoted_to_l7.fix: ima_sign uses -n -f (no setxattr; the court filesystem refuses it) and ima_verify is given the X.509 certificate in DER (evmctl 1.4 parses it with d2i_X509_fp).

promoted_to_l7.workload: affconvert + affsign/affverify over a signed AFF image, tampered image rejected
promoted_to_l7.fix: the raw source payload now has a .raw extension (AFFLIB raw_identify_file accepts .raw/.iso); the -o image path is kept.

promoted_to_l7.workload: SMTPS submission to a local peer, unrelated CA rejected
promoted_to_l7.fix: DMA reads /etc/dma/dma.conf and drops root to the `mail` user; the workload writes that path and makes the spool writable by mail. The program has no version banner, so the launch proof is an empty-output exit plus the loader closure (recorded in PROGRAMS).

promoted_to_l7.workload: HTTPS GET over verified TLS, unrelated CA rejected
promoted_to_l7.fix: correct script syntax is `_REQ host SSL:port` plus `_VERIFY_PEER`; the old script used a non-existent -f option and an _SSL:CONNECT command.

promoted_to_l7.workload: nghttp fetch from nghttpd over TLS; chain result reported
promoted_to_l7.fix: nghttp 1.64 installs a verify callback that always returns 1 and reports a failed chain only as '[WARNING] Certificate verification failed'; the workload now asserts the warning under the unrelated CA instead of a refused connection (the consumer does not refuse).

promoted_to_l7.workload: SIP call between its own UAS and UAC over verified TLS; unrelated CA rejected
promoted_to_l7.fix: the UAC now presents the fixture client certificate (SIPp always loads a default client cert) and the TLS probe no longer consumes the -m 1 UAS's only call; the negative control reads the verify error from SIPp's error log.

promoted_to_l7.workload: pki RSA keygen, X.509 issue/verify, PKCS#10, PKCS#12 parse via the openssl plugin; unrelated CA and wrong PKCS#12 password rejected
promoted_to_l7.fix: new admitted harness (forensics/tools/l7_strongswan.c) links the subject libcrypto so the L5 proof resolves it, then execs pki; the workload stages the plugin directory and makes pki print its loaded openssl/pkcs12 plugins.

promoted_to_l7.workload: dcmsign CMS SignedData (SHA-256) over a DICOM dataset; tampered dataset and unrelated CA rejected
promoted_to_l7.fix: dump2dcm input plus DCMDICTPATH; the signing certificate is valid from 2020 so the signature-creation-date check passes; verification uses +cf for the CA.

promoted_to_l7.workload: posttls-finger implicit TLS (SMTPS), TLS1.2 cipher and chain verification
promoted_to_l7.fix: the recipe stages {root}/.s36-postfix/main.cf (postfix refuses root as mail_owner); the workload opens the connection with -w (SMTPS wrapper) and reads the TLS1.2 cipher plus the chain result. Postfix passes the literal destination IP to SSL_add1_host, so the name check reports num=62 while the chain is trusted; the unrelated CA reports 'untrusted issuer'. The distinction is asserted explicitly.

blocked.blocker: charybdis refuses to run as root; the workload now drops to nobody with setpriv and stages the compiled prefix (helpers, modules, etc/logs). The daemon reaches 'Server Ready', but its ssld TLS helper returns a handshake_failure alert for every client (TLS1.2 and TLS1.3, with and without a client certificate), so no IRC greeting can be observed. No container capability was granted.
the container has no /dev/net/tun and no CAP_NET_ADMIN (TUNSETIFF is refused); unchanged from S35.

the admitted libshout build links only libogg and builds no vorbis/opus codec; its only supported format (ogg) therefore cannot accept a stream (shout_send returns SHOUTERR_INSANE after the SOURCE request). The TLS session itself is established (the peer sees the request and the wrong-host certificate is rejected), but the stream contract is unavailable in this build.
cxxtools 3.0.0 does not compile with GCC 12 (string_view static_assert); unchanged from S33.
no admitted deterministic TURN-over-TLS/DTLS allocation workload; the recipe builds turnserver but no admitted uclient exchange was written in S36.
the text client is interactive; its -d URL mode needs a staged gftprc and an FTPS fixture (AUTH TLS + PBSZ/PROT + verified data channel), which was not completed in S36.
no GSSAPI initiator/acceptor harness for the NTLMSSP mechanism was written in S36.
PKINIT needs a local KDC and an X.509 principal exchange; the recipe's admitted artifact is libk5crypto and no KDC/kinit workload was admitted in S36.
the legacy pkcs11 ENGINE needs a PKCS#11 token/provider before ENGINE_init can be exercised; no SoftHSM/Opencryptoki provider is admitted in this venue.
library-only; the HTTPS fetch + certificate-callback harness and a local smart-HTTP repository were not written in S36.
library-only; the explicit-encryption/KMS harness was not written in S36.
library-only; the Poco NetSSL C++ harness was not written in S36.

added.surface: mail client: SMTPS submission over verified TLS; the classic S/MIME PKCS#7/CMS implementation is linked against the subject
added.workload: mutt submits a message to a local SMTPS peer over TLS1.3; the message is delivered under the fixture CA and is not delivered when only the unrelated CA is trusted
added.caveat: the admitted workload drives the SMTPS/TLS path; the S/MIME CMS path is linked (smime.o / PKCS#7 through libssl) but is not driven by this workload. No CMS/S-MIME functional claim is made for mutt in S36.

not_onboarded.reason: no tractable P1000 consumer was found with a pristine, verifiable source in this batch; osslsigncode (already L7) is the only admitted consumer and its RFC3161 timestamp path is not exercised.
the P1000 has no CMP/CRMF consumer other than OpenSSL's own cmp app, which is not a downstream family; no pristine third-party source was admitted.
ngtcp2/quiche/picoquic/msquic are not P1000 families; the admitted curl/nginx/h2o builds in this venue have no QUIC backend.
the admitted OCSP-capable consumers (nginx, apache2-bin, haproxy, ruby) already have L7 rows; no new P1000 consumer with an OCSP/stapling workload was admitted in S36.
coturn (L4) is the only untried P1000 DTLS consumer in this cohort; eturnal/janus/freeradius were not built (heavy dependencies). libcoap/socat already have L7 rows.
libengine-pkcs11-openssl remains L4 (no PKCS#11 token); tpm2-tss-engine needs a TPM device; opencryptoki was not built in S36.
strongswan (now L7) loads the revocation/constraints plugins and ruby/php already verify stores/CRLs; no new P1000 consumer with a name-constraint/CRL workload was admitted in S36.

phase2.shortfall: 1 new family was added (mutt), not the requested ~30. The remaining candidate surfaces are either already represented by an admitted family, need a heavy build (freeradius/janus/eturnal/libdigidocpp), need hardware (TPM/token), or have no P1000 consumer (QUIC/CMP/TS). This is a partial Phase 2 and is not reported as a completion.

The +11 L7 count is 10 repaired/admitted workloads plus one new family, not a claim that the corpus is now stable or complete.
The Phase-2 shortfall (1 family versus ~30) is reported as a shortfall, not as a partial success.
